title: Perpetual check

D0.outcome: Explains perpetual check as a sequence of checks the king cannot escape and that repeats the position.

D1.outcome: When told 'find the perpetual', finds the checking sequence and shows the repetition.

D2.outcome: In mixed sets, finds the perpetual for the worse side, and tests the king's escape squares before relying on it.

D3.outcome: Decides whether to take the perpetual or play on, verifying the king cannot escape the checks and that a better winning try does not exist; predicts how one extra defender or flight square breaks it.

misconceptions: A series of checks is a perpetual without testing where the king can go.
A perpetual is always the best result for the worse side, and the better side should always accept it.
sources: sources/sheets/emlasker_common-sense.md §4.16 (does the perpetual exist? the champion's own error); §8 idea 9
sources/sheets/nimzowitsch_my-system.md §4 idea 13 (two rooks on the seventh; rook and knight apparatus)
sources/sheets/capablanca_chess-fundamentals.md §5 item 21 (engines often show taking the repetition)
conditions: The king has no escape from the checks, the checking piece cannot be blocked or captured, and checks repeat.
Two rooks on the seventh rank keep checking if the guarding rook stays as the sentinel.
contrasts: The checking sequence ends when the king reaches a square the checker cannot follow, so no perpetual exists.
The perpetual exists but the stronger side can avoid it by interposing or by a tactic.
A position where the worse side has a better practical try than a draw.
